one_month_reasoning: Starting point is the $64.85 after-hours price (-5.6%) following the Q3 print, not the $68.69 close. In the window: the 2026-10-21 session digests the print (Q3 beat: EPS $0.87 vs $0.82 consensus, margin 34.6%; but Q4 EPS guide $0.67 vs $0.73 consensus with a ~120bp layoff charge, ad revenue cut to ~$2.7B from ~$3B, FY FCF cut to ~$12.0B). Post-earnings drift after a guide-down is mildly negative, but the stock already sits at its 52-week low and 17x forward EPS with a large buyback running ($4.8B in Q3, $22.3B left), which tends to cushion. No other scheduled company event before 2026-11-19 (NFL Thanksgiving Eve game is 2026-11-25, after the window). So I centre at ~$65.2 (near the after-hours price) with sigma 11.5% (37% annual vol / 3.5 = 10.6%, plus some extra for the not-yet-settled earnings reaction). Round 2: unchanged; the call added no new scheduled event in the window (no FY2027 guide until the January call).

fair_value.method: Engine-valued driver set: four-region revenue build ($56.3B FY27, +10.2%) with GAAP margin 31.5% -> 36.0% by FY30; blend of P/E 18x NTM model EPS (~$4.19) $75.49 (w0.55), driver DCF at 9.3% WACC / 3% g $67.82 (w0.20), EV/EBITDA 14x $70.57 (w0.25) = $72.73 at the 2027-10-20 horizon, after a -$1.0B expected M&A adjustment.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM GAAP EPS at horizon ~$4.19 (model; consensus FY27 $3.80 / FY28 $4.52) x 18x (single-basis peer median 20.4x, gate-corrected from a mixed-basis 22.4x; NFLX today 18.2x NTM)

inputs_detail.derivation: 8-peer median NTM P/E 22.4x: peers.md DIS 15.2, FOXA 11.1, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, AMZN 28.2, TKO 35.4, plus GOOGL 340.27/14.97 = 22.7x on FY2027 (its FY2026 EPS carries stake gains, peers.md note) and SPOT 526.12/17.28 = 30.4x (Nasdaq consensus, my arithmetic). NFLX's own post-print NTM multiple: 64.85 / (Q4'26 guide $0.67 + Q1-Q3'27 consensus 0.93+0.98+0.98 = $3.56) = 18.2x. 18x holds today's discount (~20%) to the median: NFLX's FY28/FY27 consensus EPS growth (+19%, 4.52/3.80) is below the next-year growth of META (+23.5%), AMZN (+32.7%) (peers.md) and SPOT (+26.0%, 17.28/13.71), and US TV-time share is slipping to YouTube (Nielsen via AdWave); I have no evidenced catalyst for a re-rating within 12 months, so round 1's 19x is cut to 18x. Gate correction (2026-10-21, mixed basis): the 8-peer median mixed the run table's NTM fiscal-year blends with GOOGL and SPOT on calendar FY2027 alone. On one basis (peers.md NTM fiscal-year blend of Nasdaq.com/Zacks consensus EPS, Zacks basis for every name) the median is 20.4x: FOXA 11.1, DIS 15.2, WMG 18.5, META 22.2, AMZN 28.2, TKO 35.4 -> (18.5 + 22.2) / 2 = 20.35. GOOGL is dropped (its Zacks FY2026 EPS 20.55 includes non-operating stake gains); SPOT is out of the run table (EUR reporter) and on the same blend is 526.08 / (0.504 x 13.71 + 0.496 x 17.28 = 15.48) = 34.0x, which would make a 7-name median of 22.2x. The 18x multiple itself is unchanged (judgment).
inputs_detail.variant_view: At 19x the P/E leg is +$4.2 (+$2.3 on the blend); at the 22.4x median +$18.5 on the leg

thesis_break_reason: $48 is ~12.6x FY2027 consensus EPS ($3.80), ~26% below the $64.85 post-print price and at my bear value ($48.0). A close there would most likely mean earnings themselves are breaking, not only a lower multiple: revenue growth falling to mid-single digits (price rises no longer sticking, churn up), ads stuck near $3B and no margin expansion in the January FY2027 guide, or a large value-destroying acquisition. The one-sigma 12-month range at 37% vol is ~$45-95, so I place the break at the fundamental bear case rather than at ordinary volatility.

reverse_dcf_check: Engine: the blended multiples (18x P/E, 14x EV/EBITDA) imply a WACC of 8.8% on my driver path (3% terminal growth, 36.0% FY30 margin). Equivalently, holding the WACC-minus-growth spread the multiples imply (8.8% - 3%), my 9.3% WACC would need roughly 3.6% perpetual growth after FY30 to reach the multiple values (a Gordon-spread approximation, not an engine run). Plausible but not demanding given the post-horizon risks above (attention share, sports and content inflation, Paramount-WBD), which is why the multiple stays ~20% below the 22.4x peer median.

Engine values the set at $72.73 (P/E $75.49, DCF $67.82, EV/EBITDA $70.57); scenarios $48.2/$72.7/$92.5 at 25/50/25. Model NTM EPS at the horizon ~$4.19. Because the market price beats valuation blends as a 12-month forecast, the ladder is a scenario mixture with medians $49/$69/$86 (shaded toward $64.85 vs the engine values) and in-scenario sigma 0.22-0.28; total spread ~37% realized vol. P(>= $69) 0.483, P(>= $48) 0.856, P(>= $103) 0.075. model_inputs.structure_note: Value carried by: P/E (NTM at the horizon on model GAAP EPS, 18x) weight 0.55; driver DCF weight 0.20 (forward P/E 17.1x on $64.85 / FY2027 consensus $3.80 -> 15.0-19.6x band); EV/EBITDA NTM 14x weight 0.25. The round-1 SOTP leg (weight 0.15) is dropped: its advertising part at 5x EV/sales had no ad-margin or peer-ad-business evidence, and its weight goes to the two multiple legs in their 0.45:0.20 ratio. Revenue is a four-region segment build (Netflix's only reported revenue segmentation); Netflix stopped disclosing members/ARM in 2025 so each region's growth is decomposed into members, price and ads in driver_note. Region margins are not disclosed, so every region carries the company margin (no corporate line).
